record.what_it_does: API-first B2B customer support platform with AI agents and Slack/email/in-app channels.
record.auth_notes: API keys belong to machine users, carry fine-grained permissions, and are sent as "Authorization: Bearer plainApiKey_xxx". OAuth apps are created under Settings → OAuth applications and use authorization code with refresh, PKCE for client-side apps, scopes openid and offline_access, and endpoints at signin.auth.plain.com. The OAuth docs say "The app only works in the workspace you created it in." That means no multi-tenant OAuth app is available for distribution, so a multi-user toolkit would have each customer supply a per-workspace API key or create their own OAuth app. The MCP server uses OAuth login tied to the Plain user.
record.access_notes: There is no permanent free tier. Plans are Foundation ($45/user/mo), Horizon ($99/user/mo) and Frontier (custom), all billed annually. "Every plan starts with a free 7-day trial, and the trial doesn't need a credit card." Neither the pricing page nor the billing docs restrict the API, webhooks or MCP to a particular plan; the developer platform is listed generally. Lasting access needs a paid plan.
record.api_breadth_notes: GraphQL API at https://core-api.uk.plain.com/graphql/v1, with the schema published at /graphql/v1/schema.graphql. It covers customers, threads, events, labels, tiers, companies, webhook targets, API keys, billing and more. The MCP server alone exposes "nearly 400 tools", which points to a very large operation surface.
record.mcp_notes: Vendor-hosted at https://mcp.plain.com/mcp. It uses OAuth ("No API keys needed") and has the same permissions as the Plain user. The docs say "nearly 400 tools".
record.blocker_notes: There is no free tier. Testing needs a 7-day trial (no credit card) or a paid workspace. OAuth apps only work in the workspace that created them, so no shared multi-tenant OAuth app is possible and the toolkit must rely on per-workspace API keys. The API is GraphQL only, with no OpenAPI spec.
